title: Be first through the gate at the Acropolis
description: The site opens at eight and the marble is lethal in the afternoon heat. The Parthenon has been under restoration since 1975 and will be for a while yet.

title: See the Parthenon marbles that are still in Athens
description: The top floor is laid out to the exact dimensions of the Parthenon, with plaster casts standing in for the pieces held in London.

title: Walk up Lycabettus for the sunset
description: Two hundred and seventy-seven metres above the city, with the Acropolis below and the Saronic Gulf beyond. A funicular runs if you would rather.

title: Eat your way through the Varvakios market
description: The central meat and fish market, with tavernas inside it that open at dawn and serve patsas to people finishing a night shift.

title: Watch the sun go down at the Temple of Poseidon
description: A fifth-century BC temple on a headland an hour from Athens. Byron carved his name into a column, which you should not copy.

title: Test the acoustics at the theatre of Epidaurus
description: Fourteen thousand seats, and a coin dropped in the orchestra is audible in the back row. Summer festival performances still use it.

title: Walk through the Lion Gate at Mycenae
description: The citadel of Agamemnon, with a beehive tomb outside the walls that held the largest unsupported span in Europe for a thousand years.

title: Explore the ghost city of Mystras
description: A Byzantine capital abandoned on a mountainside above Sparta, with frescoed churches and a palace scattered down the slope.

title: Drive the tower villages of the Mani
description: Stone tower houses built for blood feuds, on a bare limestone peninsula that stayed effectively independent for centuries.

title: Walk the stadium at ancient Olympia
description: The original stadium track is still there and you can run the length of it. The games ran here every four years for over a millennium.

title: Stand where the oracle spoke at Delphi
description: The Greeks considered this the navel of the world. The site climbs the mountainside, so the walk up is part of it.

title: Cross the stone bridges of the Zagori
description: Forty-six slate villages linked by arched packhorse bridges, above the Vikos gorge, which is among the deepest in the world.

title: Row to the island in Lake Pamvotida
description: A lake island with no cars, monasteries and the house where Ali Pasha was finally shot through the floorboards in 1822.

title: Ride the Pelion narrow gauge train
description: A 60-centimetre gauge line designed by the father of the painter de Chirico, winding through chestnut forest to the sea.

title: Walk to the summit of Mount Olympus
description: Two thousand nine hundred and eighteen metres, with a refuge halfway and a genuine scramble on the final summit of Mytikas.

title: Eat bougatsa in Thessaloniki in the morning
description: Filo pastry with semolina custard, dusted with icing sugar and cut up with scissors. Greece's second city takes breakfast seriously.

title: See the frescoes at Kastoria's Byzantine churches
description: Fifty-four surviving Byzantine churches around a lakeside town that made its money on fur, most of them small and unlocked on request.

title: Swim in the lagoon at Balos
description: Pink-tinged sand and shallow water at the top corner of Crete, down a rough track or by boat from Kissamos.

title: Walk the palace at Knossos
description: The Minoan palace Evans partly rebuilt in concrete, controversially. Go to the Heraklion museum afterwards for the originals.

title: Ride the boat to Spinalonga
description: A Venetian fortress island used as a leper colony until 1957, and the last one in Europe to close.

title: Walk the Preveli palm gorge to the beach
description: A freshwater river running through a palm forest to a beach, which is not a combination Greece offers often.

title: Climb to the unfinished kouros of Naxos
description: A ten-metre marble statue abandoned in the quarry where it cracked, lying on its back in an orchard since the seventh century BC.

title: Take a boat to Kleftiko on Milos
description: White volcanic rock formations and sea caves used by pirates, reachable only from the water.

title: Walk the medieval street of the Knights
description: The largest inhabited medieval town in Europe, built by the Knights Hospitaller and still lived in behind four kilometres of wall.

title: Arrive into Symi harbour by boat
description: Neoclassical houses in ochre and blue stacked around a horseshoe harbour, built on sponge money and barely altered since.

title: See the cave of the Apocalypse on Patmos
description: The cave where John is said to have received the Revelation, under a fortified monastery that has run since 1088.

title: Walk to the monastery on the cliff at Amorgos
description: A white monastery three metres deep and eight storeys tall, glued to a vertical cliff three hundred metres above the sea.

title: Swim at the Canal d'Amour on Corfu
description: Soft sandstone eroded into channels and arches on the north coast, with the swim-through the whole place is named for.

title: Look down on the shipwreck at Navagio
description: A smuggler's freighter beached in 1980 on white cliffs and blue water. The clifftop viewing platform has been moved for rockfalls.

title: Row on the underground lake at Melissani
description: The cave roof collapsed, so at midday the sun drops straight onto water that reads as electric blue.

title: Walk the petrified forest of Lesbos
description: Twenty-million-year-old sequoia trunks turned to stone by volcanic ash, standing upright where they grew.

title: Swim in the vathres rock pools of Samothraki
description: Granite plunge pools fed by waterfalls off Mount Saos, on an island with no airport and very little tourism.

title: Walk up to the Panagia above Chora
description: A zigzag path from a cliff-edge village to a whitewashed church, with the Aegean two hundred metres straight down.
